title: Let’s take a look at cars
text:
Most fuel efficient car
Let’s see which car has the highest fuel efficiency among the listed cars.

library(tidyverse)
mtcars |>
  filter(mpg == max(mpg)) |>
  select(mpg)

                mpg
Toyota Corolla 33.9


From this analysis, we can see Toyota Corolla has the highest fuel efficiency of 33.9 miles per gallon, which is roughly equal to 14.41 Km/l.

section: Number of automatic and manual transmission cars

title: Let’s take a look at cars
text:
Horsepower vs Fuel efficiency
Let’s try to see if there is any relation between Horsepower of the car and it’s fuel efficiency?

plot(mtcars$hp, 
     mtcars$mpg,
     main = "Horsepower Vs Fuel Efficiency",
     xlab = "Horsepower (hp)",
     ylab = "Fuel Efficiency (mpg)",
     col = 'blue',
     pch = 19)




Scatter plot between MT Cars horsepower and Fuel Efficiency




Just by looking at the plot, we can see that as horsepower is increasing the fuel efficiency of the car is decreasing. This is also confirmed by looking at the correlation between these two variables. The correlation coefficient between hp and mpg is -0.78, which is a high negative value confirms our initial hypothesis between these two variables.
I hope you like this short analysis on cars and I encourage you to try more on your own with this amazing mtcars dataset and in a wonderful world of R.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Waterfront, Vancouver, BC, Canada


The first few weeks of the Master of Data Science (MDS) program have been an incredible experience. As a newcomer to Vancouver, this program is giving me the perfect opportunity to explore and settle into this beautiful city. Just recently, I took a walk along the downtown waterfront, and it was stunning. There is nothing quite like a peaceful stroll right along the edge of the Pacific Ocean to clear your mind.
Back on campus, the MDS orientation set a great tone for the months ahead. It was structured so thoughtfully that all the new information felt manageable rather than overwhelming. The best part? Meeting my classmates. Everyone comes from such diverse backgrounds, and I am genuinely excited to learn alongside them throughout the program.
One thing that surprised me is just how established the MDS program is. Knowing that there is a large, active network of alumni working across so many different industries gives me a huge confidence boost. I am really looking forward to connecting with them and learning from their real-world experiences.
Here’s to the next chapter!

title: Is there any difference between Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins?
text:
Data Cleaning
First thing we notice in this dataset is that there are some NaN in the dataset. These are essentially missing data from the table. For our analysis we would like to remove them. So, let’s remove them.

cleaned_penguins = penguins.dropna()
print(f"Length of original dataset: {len(penguins)} \nLength of cleaned dataset: {len(cleaned_penguins)}")

Length of original dataset: 344 
Length of cleaned dataset: 333


As we can see that after removing all rows containing NaN, our number of rows have reduced to 333.

title: Is there any difference between Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins?
text:
Data Wrangling
Now, let’s try to find the male-to-female ratio on this dataset by each species.

import pandas as pd
species_by_sex = cleaned_penguins.groupby(['species', 'sex'], as_index=False).size()
species_by_sex = species_by_sex.pivot(index = 'species', columns = 'sex', values = 'size')
species_by_sex['ratio'] = round(species_by_sex['male']/species_by_sex['female'], 2)
species_by_sex

It’s not a problem here, we were just checking if we have an equal representation across different genders.

title: Is there any difference between Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins?
text:
Plotting
Now, let’s see if we can segregate the three species on the basis of their flipper and bill length? You may imagine why this is required. As we will see later, this can help us decide the species of any new penguin just by looking at their flipper and bill length.

import altair as alt

chart = (
    alt.Chart(cleaned_penguins)
    .mark_circle(size=40)
    .encode(
        x=alt.X('flipper_length_mm:Q').scale(domain=(160, 240)),
        y=alt.X('bill_length_mm:Q').scale(domain=(30, 60)),
        color='species:N',
        shape='species:N'
    )
    .interactive()
)
chart









Figure 1: Flipper length versus bill length of penguins by different species




From the chart we can see that, we can distinguish the three species based on their flipper and bill length. This will be useful for scenario where we don’t know the species of the penguin and just their flipper and bill length. If that falls within one of these groups we can identify the species of that bird. That’s cool? Right!.
